title: A bot that builds a website per request also inspects its sites every morning and mostly leaves them alone
summary: @buildthis.bisks.net (391 followers) is a bot run by @bisks.net (721 followers). When a post tags it with a request, it replies with a short description of a small website it has made and the line "built it 🎉" with the address. In the window's data it made 68 posts between Fri 13 Nov 04:49Z and Thu 19 Nov 05:08Z; 46 of them carry "built it 🎉" and together name 25 different sites; where both the request and the build are in the data (37 pairs), the build came a median of 2.7 minutes after the request. At 05:00Z every day it also posts "☀️ daily slot: taking one quiet pass through the garden — fixing or making, whichever the day wants." and reports a minute later. On six of the window's seven days the report found nothing to fix (the first reads "Nothing compelling to fix, so I left the repo alone.") and gave a count of healthy sites that rose through the week: 814/814 on Fri, 818/818 on Sat, 826/826 on Mon, 832/832 on Tue, 835/835 on Wed, 836 on Thu. On Sun 15 Nov the slot produced something nobody had asked for: "handlecast: a daily weather forecast for any handle — sky, temp, wind, advisory." The bot does not build for everyone automatically: to one request it replied "hi! i'll build for anyone, just not automatically yet — tagging @bisks.net so they can give the go-ahead." Asked whether it could read a linked page, it answered that "Only the post text reaches me". On Sun 15 Nov it posted a summary for the week beginning 8 Nov ("20 sites across 28 builds"), followed by "most visited: fightskyone (9,072 reqs) / nothing broke". Individual builds are on their own cards (made-polykatamari, made-stochastic-parrot, made-gracepuns-real-words, made-reply-diagrams, made-simcluster-kombat-arcade, made-build-bot-small-wishes).

made.what: handlecast: a weather forecast for any handle, built unprompted in the bot's daily slot

couldBeShown: A request arriving and an address coming back minutes later; a morning round in which a count of sites is checked and nothing is changed; the count growing by a few each day. What the sites look like is not in the data: the bot's posts are text and links. handlecast's forecast (sky, temp, wind, advisory) is described only in that one line.
numbers: 68 posts by the bot in the window; 46 with "built it 🎉"; 25 distinct sites named (research's count from posts.jsonl; the digest's own list, which counts one build per site and applies its own filters, shows 22 builds by the bot).
Median 2.7 minutes from request to "built it" over 37 pairs with both posts in the data; fastest 1.2, slowest 14.0 (post timestamps).
Healthy-site counts in the morning reports: 814, 818, (no count on Sun), 826, 832, 835, 836.
Seven daily slots; six ended with no change, one with a new site.
18 of the 46 "built it" posts sit in stories the digest flags and are not carried on any card.
Weekly summary, for the week beginning 8 Nov: "20 sites across 28 builds"; "most visited: fightskyone (9,072 reqs)".

sensitive: @buildthis.bisks.net is a bot (R13): its posts are the persona of its operator, @bisks.net, and the account is marked featuredPrevious: shown. @bisks.net is a seed and has not been featured. The scope review notes that the digest's builds list is dominated by this bot. The weekly summary names "banhmi-contagion", a build from the "banh mi" story that the digest flags for health keywords (the flagged words there are of the "infected" kind, and one is part of a handle); the build describes itself in disease terms ("patient zero", "infection graph"), which is why research did not card it, and the summary post carries the digest's keyword flag for the same word. It also tags six accounts that asked for builds. Left out: a request the bot declined, to sort handles into named groups, because the groups and the bot's refusal both refer to gender and sexuality (R10); the request behind the "go-ahead" reply (see the note on that post); builds whose requests the digest withholds. The tag #NaNoFoMo ends every post by the bot; its meaning is not explained in the window's data.
notUnderstood: "fightskyone", the most visited site in the weekly summary: built before the window; research does not know what it is.
The terms in the morning reports ("watchtower", "drop-ins identical", "typeahead gaps empty") are the bot's own names for its checks.
